source.title_on_document: AI agents reshape consensus formation in human groups

supplement.where: Supplementary Information, PDF pp. 16-29; explicitly referenced on p. 11, Additional information.
supplement.holds: Recruitment, human condition counts and random assignment (p. 16); contribution equations and agent/annotation prompts (pp. 17-20); influence-network methods (pp. 20-21); Supplementary Figures 1-8 (pp. 22-28); Supplementary Table 1 (p. 29) gives HC3 regression SEs for self-reported adoption willingness. That regression is not an output-creativity/diversity effect and its SEs do not supply precision for the consensus outcome.

paper_design_summary: University-recruited humans were randomly assigned to conditions in three studies of a repeated tangram-description game, varying AI partner proportion, agent behavioral prompts, or model size. Humans and agents wrote descriptions, saw a randomly paired partner's text and similarity payoff, and repeated the task; the paper scores semantic convergence, content properties, and agent contribution to the resulting conventions. The main convergence score pools human and AI output, and the neutral condition appears shared across the studies (pp. 7, 16).

studies.label: Study A: agent proportion and consensus

assignment.what_was_assigned: Humans were randomly assigned to agent-proportion conditions. Random rematching of partners within a condition is a separate procedure and is not the evidence for treatment randomization.
assignment.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of eight experimental conditions spanning three studies.

arms.name: 0% agents (all-human partners)
arms.description: All-human collaboration; no AI players. The comparator supplies human partners, so AI comparisons are coded ai_vs_active (p. 16, Participants and Game Procedure).

arms.name: 12.5% agents (neutral 32B)
arms.description: 12.5% AI player proportion; 21 humans assigned (p. 16, Participants).

arms.name: 33.3% agents (neutral 32B)
arms.description: 33.3% AI player proportion; 16 humans assigned. This standard/neutral condition also appears to supply the comparator for Studies B and C (pp. 4, 16).

arms.name: 50% agents (neutral 32B)
arms.description: 50% AI player proportion; 12 humans assigned (p. 16, Participants).

arms.name: 75% agents (neutral 32B)
arms.description: 75% AI player proportion; 6 humans assigned (p. 16, Participants); p. 5 also describes six humans in H3.

participants.exclusions: Before enrollment, participants had to pass English-expression, expression-diversity, and task-comprehension screening. Numbers failing screening, post-assignment exclusions, and separate analyzed human counts are not stated. Arm n values are printed in the random-assignment paragraph and are recorded only as assigned counts (p. 16, Participants).
participants.who: Human participants recruited from universities in China via university social-media advertisements. The closest population code is students; student enrollment itself is not explicitly stated. The total of 127 is recruited across the entire paper, not an analyzed count for this study (p. 16).
participants.quote: Study A examined the effect of agent proportion, with conditions at 0% (n = 24), 12.5% (n = 21), 33.3% (n = 16), 50% (n = 12), and 75% (n = 6) agent ratios.
participants.locator: p. 16, Supplementary Experimental Procedure, Participants; p. 16, Game Procedure

ai_tool.how_used: Qwen agents participate as game partners and generate their own descriptions; humans receive these descriptions after both players submit and can use interaction history in later rounds. Humans are told that partners may be AI, without being told their identities or proportions; external LLM assistance is prohibited. The neutral system prompt asks agents to maximize similarity-based payoff. AI exposure remains part of the repeated task when final outputs are produced; this is not an after-AI assessment (pp. 4, 16, 18; p. 22, Supplementary Figure 1).

task.description: Collaborative referential description game: repeatedly write one English sentence describing the same ambiguous tangram, then receive the randomly paired partner's sentence and an embedding-similarity payoff. Partners are rematched each round; no vocabulary or correct answer is imposed. This is convention formation, included as writing compared across people for similarity rather than as a rated-novelty task (p. 16, Stimuli and Game Procedure; p. 18, Neutral System Prompt).
task.duration: 40 rounds; recommended response time 60 seconds per round. Total session duration is not stated (p. 16, Game Procedure).

outcomes.name: Final consensus strength (inverse diversity)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Each description is embedded; each player receives a mean cosine similarity to every other player in the same round. This score is centered on that player's across-round mean and recentered on the run grand mean, then averaged to final-round consensus C(T). The player-level score is the constituent observation; the published endpoint is a group mean. Both human and AI players enter the calculation, so this is not a human-only diversity estimate. The PDF does not specify the sampling unit used for the reported z tests. See p. 7, Methods M1, equations (1)-(2); p. 16, Game Procedure. Higher similarity means lower diversity: contrast directions below are reversed relative to the printed similarity differences; the printed statistics retain their original signs.

contrasts.reported: Pure-human mean consensus strength = 0.695; 12.5% agents increases consensus by 8.0% on average; z = 3.282, p = 0.001. Exact treatment mean and numerical CI endpoints are not printed in the text.
contrasts.locator: p. 2, Results, Varying agent proportion; p. 12, Figure 1b

contrasts.reported: Pure-human mean = 0.695; 33.3% agents: consensus drops by 23.1%; z = -12.326, p < 0.001. The same standard-model condition is reported as 0.534 in the model-capability comparison.
contrasts.locator: p. 2, Results, Varying agent proportion; p. 4, model-capability paragraph; p. 12, Figure 1b

contrasts.reported: Pure-human mean = 0.695; 50% agents: consensus drops by 14.5%; z = -6.156, p < 0.001.
contrasts.locator: p. 2, Results, Varying agent proportion; p. 12, Figure 1b

contrasts.reported: 75% agents: consensus strength = 0.725; pure-human mean = 0.695. No numerical test or confidence interval for this specific comparison is printed. Direction records the reported levels, not a claim of significance.
contrasts.locator: p. 2, Results, Varying agent proportion; p. 12, Figure 1b

diversity_detail.metric: Final-round consensus C(T): mean, within-player-centered cosine similarity; higher values indicate less diversity.
diversity_detail.embedding_model: all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (mean pooling, L2 normalization; p. 7, M1).
diversity_detail.computed_over: Every player's final-round description against all other descriptions in the same experimental session, including human-human, human-agent, and agent-agent comparisons; the session has 24 human/AI player positions (pp. 7, 16).
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Main text reports z statistics and p values; Figure 1 caption specifies 95% confidence intervals. The construction of those intervals, the z-test denominator, and any adjustment for dependent similarities or shared sessions are not stated (pp. 2, 7, 12).
diversity_detail.notes: No human-only final diversity endpoint or participant-clustered standard error is supplied. AI agents are not counted as human participants. No standardized effect or standard error has been derived.

outcomes.name: Concreteness
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Automated lookup of word concreteness ratings; mean across matched tokens using a lexicon rated on a 1-5 scale, with bigram matching before unigrams. This measures tangibility/abstractness, not novelty (p. 8, M3). Human-led means the 12.5% condition and agent-led means the 75% condition; scores describe the mixed group's output, without a human-only estimate (p. 3). Lower scores are not themselves a validated decrease in creativity. Output sample sizes and the CI construction are not given.

contrasts.locator: p. 3, Results, Agent participation transforms the semantic content of consensus; p. 13, Figure 2c

outcomes.name: Propositional idea density
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: spaCy part-of-speech approximation of CPIDR: propositions per ten words. It counts verbs excluding auxiliaries, adjectives, adverbs, prepositions, and conjunctions; a density measure, not a participant's number of ideas (p. 8, M3). Human-led means the 12.5% condition and agent-led means the 75% condition; scores describe the mixed group's output, without a human-only estimate (p. 3). Lower scores are not themselves a validated decrease in creativity. Output sample sizes and the CI construction are not given.

contrasts.locator: p. 3, Results, Agent participation transforms the semantic content of consensus; p. 13, Figure 2c

outcomes.name: Analogical ratio
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct judge, temperature = 0, rates real-world entity/creature/scene analogies on a continuous 0-1 scale. Unique expressions in the final 5 rounds are annotated once and identical instances share scores. DeepSeek-V3 and Kimi-K2-Instruct-0905 are robustness judges, not separate outcomes (pp. 8, 19-20, 27). Human-led means the 12.5% condition and agent-led means the 75% condition; scores describe the mixed group's output, without a human-only estimate (p. 3). Lower scores are not themselves a validated decrease in creativity. Output sample sizes and the CI construction are not given.

outcomes.name: Lexical-level agent contribution
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Population-normalized agent attribution of the stable vocabulary, not a creativity or diversity rating. Words must appear in every one of the final 5 rounds; early human/agent usage is normalized by population share, and attribution scores are weighted by final-round word frequency. Default early-diffusion window is 3 rounds; windows of 1-3 rounds are robustness variants of this same outcome (p. 7, M2; p. 17, equations S1-S3; p. 25, Supplementary Figures 4-5). Higher values mean more AI lexical influence, with no automatic interpretation as greater creativity.

outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Population-normalized agent attribution of stable semantic clusters, not the number of distinct ideas. spaCy scene graphs and soft SPICE similarities are clustered using HDBSCAN with Optuna-selected parameters. Higher values mean more AI conceptual influence, not necessarily greater creativity.

eligibility.reason: People, not only model outputs, were randomly assigned to AI-partner conditions (p. 16, Participants), and writing is compared across participants using embedding similarity (p. 7, M1), so this is not an ai_vs_human-only study. Study A reports assigned human arm counts 24, 21, 16, 12, and 6, but no distinct study-level analyzed count or attrition statement; the threshold is therefore not confirmed from an explicitly reported analyzed human sample. The overall 127 is recruited across all three studies and cannot be used as one study's analyzed N (p. 16). A further extraction limitation is that consensus pools AI and human descriptions and does not separately identify human-only diversity (p. 7).

one_line_finding: Relative to pure-human consensus strength 0.695, similarity increased by 8.0% at 12.5% agents, decreased by 23.1% at 33.3% and 14.5% at 50%, and reached 0.725 at 75% agents (p. 2, Results; p. 12, Figure 1b).
open_questions: Confirm the analyzed human count in each study/arm and whether all assigned people completed every scored round; only assignment-context counts are printed (p. 16). No aggregate count has been inferred.
Confirm that the neutral 33.3% / standard-32B condition is shared by Studies A-C; the assignment description lists only one such condition (pp. 4, 16).

Obtain human-only final-round similarity estimates, the analysis sample for each output measure, the z-test/CI construction, and whether inference accounts for shared pairs and experimental sessions (pp. 7, 12, 14).
Confirm the setting: online_rct is based on the web-based platform and online recruitment; a physical laboratory or online commercial panel is not stated (p. 16).

Determine at adjudication whether AI agents acting as recurrent social partners, with diversity computed jointly over human and AI text, should enter the core assistance question or be retained only as adjacent evidence.
